description: The Standard Scenarios are a suite of forward-looking scenarios of the US power sector, updated each year by the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, the former National Renewable Energy Laboratory). The page read on 2026-09-26, last updated on 20 May 2026, states that the scenarios are simulated with the Regional Energy Deployment System (ReEDS) and the Distributed Generation Market Demand model, using cost inputs from the Annual Technology Baseline, and span futures from high vehicle electrification to major technology cost declines; for selected scenarios the models are run in PLEXOS and the Cambium tool assembles hourly cost and operational data. The page names the 2024 Standard Scenarios Report and links earlier editions on the Annual Technology Baseline site. State-level results are downloaded from the Scenario Viewer and Data Downloader, whose disclaimer says the data are estimates provided for reference and subject to change; no open licence is named. Caveats: the old nrel.gov addresses no longer resolve, and scenarios are not forecasts. Simulation uses are capacity expansion, demand and generation-mix pathways for US infrastructure studies and long-run marginal emission and cost inputs. Related records: model-reeds is the capacity expansion model behind them.
